_**Agent (gpt-5.4 2026-04-01 05:03:38Z)**_

The most likely cause is a signing mismatch during your sideloaded update flow, not a Flutter UI bug.

Your app is using a fixed Android package ID, `com.example.secure_ebook_reader`, in both Gradle and Firebase, so Android treats the new APK as the same app:
[android/app/build.gradle.kts](/home/joe/Videos/Code/new/loho-ebook-reader/android/app/build.gradle.kts#L25)
[android/app/google-services.json](/home/joe/Videos/Code/new/loho-ebook-reader/android/app/google-services.json#L12)

But your `release` build is currently signed with the `debug` key:
[android/app/build.gradle.kts](/home/joe/Videos/Code/new/loho-ebook-reader/android/app/build.gradle.kts#L39)

That becomes a problem when users already have an older install signed with a different certificate, such as:
- a Play Store build
- a previous release keystore
- another APK signed on a different machine

Android then blocks the update and shows errors like: `App not installed as package conflicts with an existing package.`

Your update flow also confirms this is happening in the sideload path, because it falls back to a custom backend download when Play Store update is not used:
[lib/screens/dashboard_screen.dart](/home/joe/Videos/Code/new/loho-ebook-reader/lib/screens/dashboard_screen.dart#L325)

What to fix:
- Sign all release/update APKs with the same permanent release keystore.
- Do not ship update APKs signed with the debug key.
- Use a real unique app ID instead of `com.example...` before wider distribution.

The `Done` part is likely just your installer flow finishing after Android rejected the package, not proof the update succeeded.

If you want, I can set up proper Android release signing in this project and show you exactly what to change.

```diff
+# Android Release Signing
+
+This project now supports proper Android release signing through `android/key.properties`.
+
+## Why this matters
+
+Android only allows an installed app to be updated by another APK or AAB signed with the same certificate.
+
+If users already have your app installed and the new build is signed with a different key, Android rejects the update with errors like:
+
+`App not installed as package conflicts with an existing package.`
+
+## One-time setup
+
+1. Create or restore the release keystore you intend to keep using for all future updates.
+2. Place the keystore file somewhere under `android/`, for example:
+
+`android/app/upload-keystore.jks`
+
+3. Create `android/key.properties` with this content:
+
+```properties
+storePassword=YOUR_STORE_PASSWORD
+keyPassword=YOUR_KEY_PASSWORD
+keyAlias=upload
+storeFile=app/upload-keystore.jks
+```
+

```diff
+# Android Release Signing
+
+This project now supports proper Android release signing through `android/key.properties`.
+
+## Why this matters
+
+Android only allows an installed app to be updated by another APK or AAB signed with the same certificate.
+
+If users already have your app installed and the new build is signed with a different key, Android rejects the update with errors like:
+
+`App not installed as package conflicts with an existing package.`
+
+## One-time setup
+
+1. Create or restore the release keystore you intend to keep using for all future updates.
+2. Place the keystore file somewhere under `android/`, for example:
+
+`android/app/upload-keystore.jks`
+
+3. Create `android/key.properties` with this content:
+
+```properties
+storePassword=YOUR_STORE_PASSWORD
+keyPassword=YOUR_KEY_PASSWORD
+keyAlias=upload
+storeFile=app/upload-keystore.jks
+```
+
+## Create a new keystore
+
+If you do not already have one, generate it with:
+
+```bash
+keytool -genkeypair -v \
+  -keystore android/app/upload-keystore.jks \
+  -keyalg RSA \
+  -keysize 2048 \
+  -validity 10000 \
+  -alias upload
+```
+
+## Important
+
+- If users already installed older APKs, you must sign updates with the same original keystore used for those APKs.
+- If the previous installed app came from Google Play, updates should normally continue through Google Play.
+- If the old keystore is lost, existing sideloaded installs usually cannot be updated in place and may require uninstalling first.
+
+## Build commands
+
+```bash
+flutter build apk --release
+```
+
+or
+
+```bash
+flutter build appbundle --release
+```
```

Yes. In fact, your app already has most of that flow.

Right now it checks a backend version endpoint at [lib/screens/dashboard_screen.dart](/home/joe/Videos/Code/new/loho-ebook-reader/lib/screens/dashboard_screen.dart#L325). It reads:
- `build_number`
- `download_url`
- `mandatory`
- `release_notes`

Then if the server build is newer than the installed build, it shows a dialog and opens the APK link:
[lib/screens/dashboard_screen.dart](/home/joe/Videos/Code/new/loho-ebook-reader/lib/screens/dashboard_screen.dart#L358)
[lib/screens/dashboard_screen.dart](/home/joe/Videos/Code/new/loho-ebook-reader/lib/screens/dashboard_screen.dart#L421)

You also already have a hardcoded APK URL in settings:
[lib/screens/settings_screen.dart](/home/joe/Videos/Code/new/loho-ebook-reader/lib/screens/settings_screen.dart#L32)

The key point is this:
- The app should not check only the APK file URL.
- It should check a small JSON or API endpoint that tells it what the latest version is, and where to download the APK.

A good setup is:
```json
{
  "version": "1.2.6",
  "build_number": 126,
  "download_url": "https://yourdomain.com/app-release.apk",
  "mandatory": false,
  "release_notes": "Bug fixes and improvements."
}
```

Then the app:
1. Reads its installed build number.
2. Calls that URL/API.
3. Compares versions.
4. Opens the APK download link if newer.

So the answer is yes, and your app already does it in principle. What matters now is making sure:
- your server endpoint always returns the newest APK metadata
- the APK at `download_url` is signed with the same release key
- `pubspec.yaml` version/build number increases for each release

If you want, I can take the next step and make this cleaner by moving the update check into a dedicated service and supporting a simple hosted JSON file instead of depending on a PHP endpoint.
